normalization_detail: peak throughput = 1.0 by construction; this is a relative shape only, NOT an absolute optical/quantum efficiency

analytic_model.definition: T(lambda)=1 for lambda in [center-FWHM/2, center+FWHM/2], else 0; endpoints included

provenance.source: Astrodon 50mm H-alpha (3 nm) vendor nominal bandpass, as stated in testdata/M42_T2T3_mosaic_Flying_dutchman/素材信息与版权约定.txt
provenance.curve_origin: parameterised ideal top-hat; NOT a measured transmission curve
provenance.science_basis: docs/science/foundation/GAIA_RESPONSE.md §2: narrowband default T=1_[c-Delta/2,c+Delta/2], must be named top_hat_approx

identifiable: relative in-band spectral weighting: any spectrum is weighted equally (unit) inside [654.8,657.8] nm and zero outside
band edges and centre to the precision of the vendor nominal values (0.1 nm grid)
ratios of photon integrals within the same assumed band shape (e.g. line-to-continuum within the band)
not_identifiable: absolute throughput/QE: unit peak fixes scale arbitrarily; absolute photon rate or flux zero point cannot be derived
real passband shape: Astrodon curves have skirts, finite out-of-band transmission and incidence-angle/blue-shift dependence; the top-hat has none
out-of-band blocking: no measurement, so e.g. [OIII] or continuum leakage outside 654.8-657.8 nm cannot be bounded from this file
detector QE wavelength dependence and optics throughput separately (they are lumped in 'throughput' and set to 1)
absolute H-alpha line flux calibration and AB/photometric zero point
usage_note: Suitable for relative band integration and for weighting XP spectra inside the nominal band under the stated top-hat assumption. Must not be used as an absolute efficiency or to claim measured Astrodon response. Any absolute photometric statement needs an external calibration and a measured curve.
